title: Gmail Mailchimp Integration: How to Set It Up (2026)
summary: Gmail Mailchimp integration watches your email for events and updates your mailing list automatically. Build this workflow without writing any code.
body_markdown:
## Build the enquiry-to-subscriber workflow in Activepieces


To build it, you connect both accounts, add the trigger, add the action, then test and publish. None of that needs the HTTP fallback, because Activepieces lists a Gmail trigger and a Mailchimp action that cover this handoff.


You can also skip the clicking: describe the handoff in plain language to the built-in chat, for instance "when an email arrives under the enquiry label, add the sender to my audience", and it builds and publishes the flow for you.


What it publishes is a live flow in your account, the same kind of flow the four stages below produce, and each execution leaves a run trace showing exactly what happened.


It runs under the same RBAC and audit logs as a flow built by hand, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### Stage 1: connect Gmail and Mailchimp


Before opening the builder, create a Gmail filter on` to:[\[email protected\]](https://www.activepieces.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)` that applies a label such as` enquiry` . The label keeps newsletters and replies out of the flow, so only real enquiries reach Mailchimp.


In Activepieces, open Connections, add Gmail and approve the Google consent screen, then add Mailchimp and authorise it. Both should show as connected before you build anything.


### Stage 2: add the Gmail trigger and load sample data


Create a new flow and choose the Gmail integration's New Email trigger. Select your Gmail connection and restrict it to the` enquiry` label if the trigger offers that field. Then use the load sample data option.


If your inbox has no matching message, send yourself one first, because the trigger polls rather than fires instantly and the sample comes from a real email.


Open the sample and confirm you can see the sender address, the sender name and the subject. Those are the values you map next.


### Stage 3: add the Mailchimp action and map fields


Add the Mailchimp integration's Add or Update Subscriber action. If your version words it differently, pick the action that adds a subscriber to an audience. Fill the fields in this order:


1. Choose the audience that should receive enquirers.
2. Map the email field to the sender address from the Gmail step.
3. Map the first name to the sender name, if the action exposes a name field.
4. Set the status to subscribed only if the person has agreed to marketing. Otherwise use a transactional or pending status, so an enquiry isn't treated as consent.


On the canvas below, a step sits between a trigger and a mail action. A loop feeds an Ask AI step set to the Anthropic provider, and its output goes to Gmail's Send Email.


The Model field still reads Select an option, and that step won't run until you pick one. You would insert a step like this between Stages 2 and 3 only if you wanted to clean up the sender name before it reaches Mailchimp.


With the fields mapped, the flow is ready to test.


### Stage 4: test, check Mailchimp, publish


Run the test on the Mailchimp step, using the sample from Stage 2. Then open your audience in Mailchimp and look for the contact. A real address and name in the audience means the flow works.


If the contact is missing, check the status you set and whether the address already existed. Once it appears, publish the flow, send one fresh email to the enquiries address, and watch the run complete.
